correctness.rationale: Exact scaled error updates give the rank-one 2×2 block M with det M=0 and trace 1-alpha*rho*(a+b)/((rho+a)*(rho+b)). Cayley–Hamilton yields M²=(tr M) M; any nonzero trace creates a persistent eigenmode, whereas zero traces annihilate all modes in at most two cycles. Solving tr=0 is exactly ab=tau(a+b)-rho² with tau=rho(alpha-1) and 0<tau<=rho. The KKT z-optimality gives rho u^+=B z^+ in error coordinates. Independently recomputed exact Fraction modal matrices for (a,b)=(1,5),(2,6), rho=4, alpha=15/8: [[5/18,-2/9],[25/72,-5/18]] and [[3/20,-1/10],[9/40,-3/20]], both square to zero.
residual_risks: Exact arithmetic only; noncommuting/nonpositive Hessians, matrix penalties, floating-point termination excluded.

value.rationale: The result identifies exactly when one practical scalar penalty and over-relaxation parameter annihilate every heterogeneous quadratic coordinate, with sharp necessary and sufficient geometric conditions and two-step termination; useful for algorithm design and tests without requiring an arbitrary new algorithm.
residual_risks: Hypotheses require simultaneous diagonalization in the original scalar Euclidean metric; excludes numerical robustness.

final_claim: For positive diagonal Hessians A,B and a common scalar Euclidean ADMM penalty rho, finite termination from every (z,u) initialization under fixed standard 0<alpha<=2 occurs iff all (a_i+b_i,a_i b_i) lie on p=tau s-rho^2 for one 0<tau<=rho; alpha=1+tau/rho. All errors vanish by the second completed cycle.
limitations: Single original-coordinate scalar penalty, fixed rho and alpha, positive diagonal Hessians; no noncommuting, singular, varying-parameter, or finite-precision classification.
